I need to make a legal Monopoly move. The previous trade was invalid because properties have houses. I can end the turn, propose a new trade, unmortgage property, build or sell houses, or sell a house.

I am player two in a one-on-one game. I have $2166 and six properties with four houses each. Two railroads are mortgaged. I hold two get-out-of-jail cards.

Player one has $94 and heavily mortgaged holdings. The bank has no houses left. Building hotels on my properties would return twelve houses to the bank, which player one could then use to liquidate their hotels or build. I should avoid building hotels.

Player one cannot sell their hotels. Downgrading a hotel requires four houses from the bank, and the bank currently has none. Building hotels on my properties would therefore not let player one liquidate their holdings.

Player one can sell houses without bank houses. Selling eight red houses yields about $600. Eight light blue houses add more cash. This liquidity is independent of the hotel concern.

Standard Monopoly rules require four houses in the bank to replace a hotel before it can be sold. Player one cannot downgrade their Connecticut hotel or Boardwalk hotel without those houses. Light blue houses sell for $25 each, and dark blue houses sell for $100 each.

The even-build rule likely applies to selling as well. Hotels count as five houses, so player one would need to sell from the highest holdings first when breaking down buildings.

Player one's total liquidity is roughly $1034. Selling all red houses yields $600, and mortgaging the remaining railroads adds about $340 on top of their $94 cash. The pink properties at four houses each pay $625 in rent.

Virginia Avenue pays $700 in rent. Player one could cover St. Charles and States Avenue with their cash plus red house sales, but Virginia would leave them about six dollars short. They could mortgage a red property to cover that gap, though they must sell all buildings before mortgaging.
